sentence: This project studies how sensory cues and hormones change neurons to guide parenting and how parenting holds back competing drives.
This project provides lipid mass spectrometry measurements that show how lipids are made and broken down in cultured cells and living animals.
This project tries to find out why past drug efforts aimed at an ion channel protein failed and builds tools to guide future ones.
This project tests whether a stress-response kinase can serve as a biomarker or a therapeutic target for atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery.
This project studies how membrane curvature controls biochemical signals in cells and builds nanoscale electrodes that record action potentials in heart cells.
This project studies how an animal model regenerates entire neural subnetworks, from sensing injury to regained activity, to learn the basic principles of neuroregeneration.
This project uses information from individuals, computer programs and mouse models to find genes that cause diaphragmatic hernias and cardiovascular malformations.
This project studies how inflammatory signals from heart muscle cells activate cardiac fibroblasts through macrophages in dilated cardiomyopathy, using organoids and mouse models.
This project studies tumor macrophages that express the Autoimmune Regulator gene and how they help tumors evade immune responses.
This project makes a public skin imaging archive easier to find, access and reuse and adds clinical images and total body photography.
This project builds platforms that grow living cells in 3D cultures that mimic tissues, with remote control and analysis, for genomic studies of live cells.
This project builds tools to target harmful immune cells that drive autoimmune diseases.
This project builds a bioengineered scaffold that guides cells in the fetal environment to regenerate missing vertebral arches in spina bifida before birth.
This project builds a sequencing method that quickly and sensitively identifies the pathogens behind infectious diseases from clinical samples.
This project builds a phage cocktail, chosen with machine learning and pharmacokinetic modeling, to kill drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteria.
This project studies the molecular features, origins and disease effects of hard-to-detect structural variants in rare genetic diseases.
This project improves a smartphone app that records speech and tests whether speech biomarkers can assess depression in a community sample.
This project uses single cell analysis to study how immune cells in glioblastoma change during radiation and chemotherapy in patient samples and mouse models.
This project studies how the parent a gene variant comes from affects retinoblastoma, using long-read sequencing that captures genetic and epigenetic changes.
This project develops chemical approaches to study where RNA modifications sit in cells and how RNA interacts with proteins and small molecules.
